items.title: Section: Who Should Never Be Chosen as a Preceptor — Lacking Genuine Faith or Lineage

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不從一切唯聰慧者求受菩薩所受淨戒。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not seek to receive the pure bodhisattva precepts from just anyone merely clever in worldly terms.

items.zh: 無淨信者，不應從受；謂於如是所受淨戒初無信解，不能趣入，不善思惟。
items.en: One should not receive ordination from someone lacking genuine faith — meaning someone who, regarding these pure precepts, holds no real settled confidence at all, unable to genuinely enter into their meaning or reflect on it well.

items.title: Section: Six Missing Seed-Natures That Disqualify a Preceptor

items.zh: 有慳貪者，慳貪弊者，有大欲者，無喜足者，不應從受。毀淨戒者，於諸學處無恭敬者，於戒律儀有慢緩者，不應從受。
items.en: One should not receive ordination from someone stingy, gripped by stinginess and greed, endlessly desirous, or never satisfied. Nor from someone who has violated pure discipline, shows no reverence towards the teachings, or is careless and lax about their own conduct.

items.zh: 有忿恨者，多不忍者，於他違犯不堪耐者，不應從受。有嬾惰者，有懈怠者，多分耽著日夜睡樂、倚樂、臥樂，好合徒侶樂喜談者，不應從受。心散亂者，下至不能搆牛乳頃善心一緣住修習者，不應從受。有闇昧者，愚癡類者，極劣心者，誹謗菩薩素怛纜藏、及菩薩藏摩怛履迦者，不應從受。
items.en: Nor from someone who holds grudges, habitually retaliates, or cannot accept another's apology. Nor from someone lazy, sluggish, given to indulging in sleep, reclining, or lying down day and night, and preferring idle company and chatter. Nor from someone so scattered in mind that they cannot hold a single wholesome object even for the time it takes to milk a cow. Nor from someone dull-witted, confused, of exceedingly weak understanding, or who slanders the Great Vehicle's own scriptures and their commentaries.

items.title: Section: Why the Teaching Should Not Be Carelessly Shown to the Hostile and Faithless

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於受菩薩戒律儀法，雖已具足受持究竟，而於謗毀菩薩藏者無信有情，終不率爾宣示開悟。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, even having genuinely and fully fulfilled their own bodhisattva precepts, never carelessly explain or reveal the teaching to a being who slanders the Great Vehicle's own scriptures and holds no faith in them.

items.zh: 所以者何？
為其聞已不能信解，大無知障之所覆蔽，便生誹謗。由誹謗故，如住菩薩淨戒律儀，成就無量大功德藏，彼誹謗者亦為無量大罪業藏之所隨逐，乃至一切惡言、惡見及惡思惟未永棄捨，終不免離。
items.en: Because, hearing it, they would be unable to believe or understand it, covered over by a great obstruction of ignorance, and would instead give rise to slander. Through that slander, exactly as abiding in the bodhisattva precepts accumulates a boundless treasury of merit, the one who slanders accumulates an equally boundless treasury of grave unwholesome karma instead — one they cannot escape for as long as the underlying wrong speech, wrong view, and wrong thinking remain unabandoned.

items.title: Section: How to Properly Ordain — Teaching First, Testing Genuine Motivation

items.zh: 又諸菩薩欲授菩薩菩薩戒時，先應為說菩薩法藏摩怛履迦、菩薩學處及犯處相，令其聽受，以慧觀察自所意樂，堪能思擇受菩薩戒，非唯他勸、非為勝他。
items.en: Bodhisattvas wishing to confer the bodhisattva precepts should first explain the Great Vehicle's own scriptures and commentaries, the content of bodhisattva discipline, and what constitutes a violation, letting the candidate hear and absorb it, examining their own motivation with genuine wisdom, and confirming they are genuinely capable of deliberately choosing to receive the precepts — not merely because urged by someone else, nor in order to outdo another.

items.zh: 當知是名堅固菩薩堪受菩薩淨戒律儀，以受戒法如應正授。
items.en: Such a candidate should be understood as a genuinely resolute bodhisattva, truly capable of receiving the pure bodhisattva precepts, to whom the precepts should then be properly conferred according to the correct procedure.

items.title: Section: The Four Root Violations — Why They Are Called "Conquering," and Graded by Severity

items.zh: 如是菩薩住戒律儀，有其四種他勝處法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in restraint discipline are subject to four kinds of root violation.

items.zh: 何等為四？

items.title: Section: Root Violation One — Self-Praise and Disparaging Others Out of Craving

items.zh: 若諸菩薩為欲貪求利養恭敬，自讚毀他。是名第一他勝處法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, out of craving for material support and honour, praise themselves while disparaging others — this is the first root violation.

items.title: Section: Root Violation Two Opens — Withholding Generosity From Genuine Need

items.zh: 若諸菩薩現有資財，性慳財故，有苦、有貧、無依、無怙正求財者來現在前，不起哀憐而修惠捨；正求法者來現在前，性慳法故，雖現有法而不給施。是名第二他勝處法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, possessing genuine material means, out of sheer stinginess, feel no compassion and offer no generosity when someone genuinely suffering, poor, without support, or without protection comes with a legitimate request — or who, possessing the teaching itself, out of sheer stinginess, refuse to give it to a genuine seeker despite having it to give — this is the second root violation.

items.title: Section: Root Violation Three — Cultivated Hostility Escalating Into Violence

items.zh: 若諸菩薩長養如是種類忿纏，由是因緣，不唯發起麁言便息；由忿蔽故，加以手足、塊石、刀杖、捶打、傷害、損惱有情。內懷猛利忿恨意樂，有所違犯他來諫謝，不受、不忍、不捨怨結。是名第三他勝處法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who cultivate this kind of gripping anger, so that harsh words alone no longer satisfy it, and, overwhelmed by anger, go on to strike, injure, or otherwise harm a being with hand, foot, stone, or weapon — holding an intense, resentful hostility within, and, when another comes to remonstrate or to apologise, refuse to accept it, refuse to relent, and refuse to release the resulting grudge — this is the third root violation.

items.title: Section: Root Violation Four — Slandering the Mahāyāna Scriptures With False Teaching

items.zh: 若諸菩薩謗菩薩藏，愛樂宣說、開示、建立像似正法，於像似法或自信解，或隨他轉。是名第四他勝處法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who slander the Great Vehicle's own scriptures, delighting in teaching, expounding, and establishing a mere counterfeit of the genuine teaching, whether believing it themselves or simply adopting it from someone else — this is the fourth root violation.

items.title: Section: A Genuine Bodhisattva, or Merely a Semblance? The Four Root Violations Close

items.zh: 如是名為菩薩四種他勝處法。菩薩於四他勝處法隨犯一種，況犯一切，不復堪能於現法中增長攝受菩薩廣大菩提資糧，不復堪能於現法中意樂清淨。是即名為相似菩薩，非真菩薩。
items.en: These are called a bodhisattva's four root violations. A bodhisattva who violates even one of these four, let alone all of them, becomes unable to further increase and gather the vast provisions for awakening in this very life, and unable to attain the purified aspiration of one who has entered the great grounds — such a person is called a semblance of a bodhisattva, not a genuine one.

items.title: Section: Only the Gravest Violations Actually Cause Loss of the Vow

items.zh: 菩薩若用軟、中品纏毀犯四種他勝處法，不捨菩薩淨戒律儀；上品纏犯，即名為捨。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who violate any of the four root precepts in a mild or moderate degree do not thereby lose the bodhisattva precepts; only a violation committed in a severe degree is called a genuine loss.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩毀犯四種他勝處法，數數現行，都無慚愧，深生愛樂，見是功德，當知說名上品纏犯。
items.en: If bodhisattvas violate any of the four root precepts repeatedly, feeling no shame or remorse whatsoever, taking genuine delight in it, and regarding it as somehow virtuous — this should be understood as a violation in its severe degree.

items.title: Section: Unlike Monastic Ordination, a Fallen Bodhisattva Can Receive the Precepts Again

items.zh: 非諸菩薩暫一現行他勝處法，便捨菩薩淨戒律儀。如諸苾芻犯他勝法，即便棄捨別解脫戒。
items.en: It is not the case that a bodhisattva who commits even a single, occasional instance of a root violation thereby loses the bodhisattva precepts entirely — unlike a monk, who upon committing a comparable grave violation immediately and permanently loses the individually liberating precepts.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩由此毀犯，棄捨菩薩淨戒律儀，於現法中堪任更受，非不堪任。如苾芻住別解脫戒，犯他勝法，於現法中不任更受。
items.en: Even should a bodhisattva, through such a violation, genuinely lose the bodhisattva precepts, they remain fully capable of receiving them again in this very life — unlike a monk who, having lost the individually liberating precepts through a comparable grave violation, can never receive them again in this life.

items.title: Section: Only Two Things Truly End the Bodhisattva Vow — And It Survives Every Rebirth

items.zh: 略由二緣，捨諸菩薩淨戒律儀。一者、棄捨無上正等菩提大願；二者、現行上品纏犯他勝處法。
items.en: The bodhisattva precepts are lost, in brief, through only two conditions: first, abandoning the great vow towards unsurpassed, perfect awakening; second, committing a root violation in its severe degree.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，雖復轉身遍十方界，在在生處不捨菩薩淨戒律儀；由是菩薩不捨無上菩提大願，亦不現行上品纏犯他勝處法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, even passing through countless rebirths across the ten directions, do not lose the bodhisattva precepts in any of those lives, so long as they do not abandon the great vow towards unsurpassed awakening, and do not commit a root violation in its severe degree.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩轉受餘生，忘失本念，值遇善友，為欲覺悟菩薩戒念，雖數重受而非新受，亦不新得。
items.en: Should a bodhisattva, reborn into a new life, genuinely forget having ever taken this vow, and later encounter a good friend who helps awaken that same memory of the bodhisattva precepts, receiving them again, though it happens again and again across many lives, is never truly a new reception — nothing genuinely new is gained that was not already there.

blocks.text: The qualifications of a preceptor, and the **four root violations** (四他勝處法) of the bodhisattva precepts. Fascicle 40 ends today.

Not someone "merely clever in worldly terms"; not someone lacking real faith in these precepts; not someone stingy, a precept-breaker, holding grudges ("cannot accept another's apology"), lazy ("indulging in sleep day and night"), scattered, or foolish.
The teaching is not revealed to one who slanders the Mahāyāna scriptures: "hearing it, they could not believe it", and slandering it would harm them.

"First explain the scriptures, the content of bodhisattva discipline, and what constitutes a violation." Test the candidate's motive. Master Cháng Bǎi: four causes of violation: ignorance, negligence, intense affliction, disrespect.

items: "Out of craving for support and honour, praising oneself and disparaging others."
"Possessing means, out of stinginess, offering no help to someone suffering and without support"; likewise withholding the Dharma.
Anger that "harsh words alone no longer satisfy", leading to striking and harming, and "refusing an apology".
"Slandering the bodhisattva canon", teaching a counterfeit.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: they are called "defeating" because affliction defeats the mind.

subs.head: Only severe violations end the vow

blocks.text: A mild or moderate violation does not lose the precepts; a severe one ("repeatedly, without shame, delighting in it, regarding it as virtuous") does. But "unlike a monk, a bodhisattva who loses the precepts can receive them again in this very life".

"Abandoning the great vow, or a root violation of the severe degree." Otherwise "even through countless rebirths they are not lost". If one forgets them in a new life, one may receive them again; "this is not a new reception".
The heart of bodhisattva ethics: three storehouses, the ceremony, and the four root violations. Fascicle 41 continues with the lighter offences.

options: relying on it one develops great wisdom; without its explanations, the scripture's meaning cannot be clear
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: taking it as the root, one develops great wisdom — hence "root-mother." Master Cháng Bǎi: without the word-by-word explanation of the mātṛkā (treatises), the scriptures' meaning cannot be made clear.

quiz.q: From what kind of person does the treatise say bodhisattvas do not seek the precepts?
options: anyone merely clever; Cháng Bǎi: a worldly scholar may speak eloquently yet lack even the refuges and five precepts
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas do not seek to receive the pure bodhisattva precepts from just anyone merely clever." Master Cháng Bǎi: some worldly scholars, without precepts, can still explain the dharma eloquently, but one cannot receive the precepts from them. Venerable Miào Jìng notes the treatise does not say the preceptor must be a monastic.

quiz.q: Before conferring the bodhisattva precepts, what does the treatise say to do first?
options: first explain the scriptures and commentaries, the precepts, and what counts as violation, so the candidate examines their own motive with wisdom — not merely urged by others, not to outdo others
quiz.why: The preceptor "should first explain the Great Vehicle's own scriptures and commentaries, the content of bodhisattva discipline, and what constitutes a violation." Master Cháng Bǎi: not because others urged it, not because the teacher required it, and not to outdo others.

quiz.q: In "the four dharmas of being conquered by the other," what is "the other"?
options: affliction, unwholesome dharmas; when they conquer the mind and a grave precept is broken, it is called "conquered by the other"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "the other" is affliction — unwholesome dharmas; when they defeat the mind and a grave precept is broken, it is called a dharma of being conquered by the other. Venerable Miào Jìng: what is "the other"? Unwholesome dharmas.

quiz.q: What is the first root violation?
options: out of craving for support and honour, praising oneself while disparaging others
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas who, out of craving for material support and honour, praise themselves while disparaging others — this is the first root violation." Master Cháng Bǎi: self-praise alone or disparaging others alone is a minor offence; both together is grave. Its root affliction is greed.

quiz.q: What is the fourth root violation?
options: slandering the bodhisattva scriptures and delighting in teaching and establishing a counterfeit dharma
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas who slander the Great Vehicle's own scriptures, delighting in teaching, expounding, and establishing a mere counterfeit of the genuine teaching." Master Cháng Bǎi: forming a mistaken conviction in false teaching oneself is "believing it oneself"; clinging to it after hearing it from others is "adopting it from someone else."

quiz.q: What makes a root violation one committed "in the severe degree"?
options: repeatedly, without any shame, with delight, regarding it as virtuous
quiz.why: "If bodhisattvas violate any of the four root precepts repeatedly, feeling no shame or remorse whatsoever, taking genuine delight in it, and regarding it as somehow virtuous — this should be understood as a violation in its severe degree." Venerable Miào Jìng: if you break the precept but don't regard it as virtuous, it is not the severe grade of affliction.
